summary.en: Phanariot officer in the Russian army and leader of the Filiki Eteria from 1820. He opened the revolution by crossing into Moldavia in February 1821, in an expedition that collapsed within four months.

body_html.en:
Ypsilantis was born into one of the great Phanariot families of Constantinople and lost an arm fighting for Russia at Dresden in 1813. In 1820 he accepted the leadership of the Filiki Eteria, the secret society preparing a Greek rising, after Kapodistrias had declined it.

His crossing of the Pruth into Moldavia on 6 March 1821 was meant to draw Russia into the war. It did not. Disowned by the Tsar and defeated at Drăgășani in June, he fled into Austrian territory and was imprisoned for six years. He died in Vienna a few weeks after his release, as the Greek state he had helped to start was taking shape without him.
